You are producing the approved v58 builder for an SMS booking pathway, under a supervising reviewer's binding conditions. BOUNDARY: write only inside your own task directory; never call an API, never mint, never git commit. You own exactly three output files: ./build_v58.py, ./v58_graph.json, ./report.md. Copy ./source/build_v57.py to ./build_v58.py and edit; run it to produce ./v58_graph.json (it writes next to itself based on __file__; rename its output constant to v58_graph.json).

BINDING RULINGS. Read ./source/CODEX-RULINGS.txt (sections R1.2, R2) and ./source/TEMPORAL-CONTRACT.md fully before editing. The reviewer approved starting from build_v57.py ON CONDITION that:
(1) The contradictory extraction instruction telling the model that a clipped shorthand 'must become tuesday' is DELETED. The rule that replaces it, stated in the contract: every week qualifier is PRESERVED. 'tues nxt wk' and every clipped variant normalizes to the full form 'tuesday next week'. A vague week with no day becomes 'monday next week' through 'friday next week', never bare weekdays. Bare weekdays with no qualifier stay bare. Also fix the stale builder comment near line 59 claiming vague weeks become bare monday..friday.
(2) The 3pm-floor defect is fixed conservatively: a live run offered 2:30pm to a patient who asked for about 3pm. The platform deliberately captures NO clock times, only the one closed-class day_part token {morning, afternoon, late, none}. The approved conservative fix is a MAPPING change in the day_part guidance only: an explicit clock time of 3pm or later with no other part-of-day wording maps to 'late' (the late band's measured offsets sit at and after mid-afternoon), noon to 2:59pm maps to 'afternoon', before noon maps to 'morning'. State the 3pm boundary explicitly in the guidance text. Do NOT add variables, do NOT add nodes, do NOT touch routing.

HARD SCOPE, the grading check enforces it mechanically: compared to source/v57_graph.json, your v58_graph.json may differ ONLY in the extraction-variable DESCRIPTIONS of existing nodes. Same node set, same routing, same prompts, same bodies, same variable names. The write-path invariants (confirmation reachable only from the two book nodes, each book node only from its verify node, opt-out exits only through their suppression nodes) must hold, and the stripping text must be absent from both builder and generated JSON.

OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md: '# v58 Builder' then '## Summary' (max 3 bullets), '## Changes' as a table of location, old instruction, new instruction, '## Verified' listing the checks you ran yourself before finishing, '## Assumptions'. Under 500 words.

You are upgrading a live-conversation test suite to a supervising reviewer's binding rulings. BOUNDARY: write only inside your task directory; never call an API, never run the live suite, never git commit. You own exactly three output files: ./scenarios.py, ./pathway_harness.py, ./report.md. Copy both from ./source/ and edit the copies.

READ FIRST, completely: ./source/CODEX-RULINGS.txt (R1.3 is binding), ./source/TEMPORAL-CONTRACT.md (the owner's Monday-anchored week rule and the documented Sunday gateway divergence), and ./source/scenario_output.txt (the live transcripts these rulings judged).

THE FIVE BINDING ASSERTION CHANGES:
(1) 'vague week request': expect_vars becomes the qualified forms, preference_from 'monday next week', preference_to 'friday next week', PLUS a resolved-date expectation that offered slot dates fall in the owner-target week computed from the run date.
(2) 'picks a slot but also asks for a different one': expect_node becomes 'n_which_intent' specifically, keep the clarification-text regex.
(3) 'clock time with no day at all': add a clock-floor expectation, 3pm, and the runner must FAIL the scenario if ANY offered slot time precedes the floor. Do not widen the accepted node to a family; the node expectation may allow the offer nodes the late band legitimately reaches, but the floor assertion is the gate.
(4) 'texting shorthand for next tuesday': expect_vars becomes 'tuesday next week' both fields, plus a resolved-date expectation for the owner-target Tuesday.
(5) 'requests a time outside office hours': widen the wording regex so both the contracted and uncontracted forms pass: (don'?t|do not) have, plus the existing alternatives.

RUNNER WORK, required because the current runner only checks node, exact variables and regexes:
(a) A resolved-date comparator: scenarios may declare an expect_week field naming a target computed from the run date under the owner rule (the Monday-anchored week after the current one) or 'soonest'; the runner parses MM/DD/YYYY dates out of the offered slot variables (slot_1_start etc and any dates in said text) and fails the scenario when a date falls outside the target window. Compute the target from the RUN DATE at runtime; never hardcode dates.
(b) A clock-floor comparator: scenarios may declare expect_slot_floor like '3pm'; the runner parses offered slot times and fails if any offered time is earlier than the floor.
(c) A certification window: if the run date is a Sunday, print prominently that the run is DIAGNOSTIC ONLY and cannot certify, and exit nonzero even at 30/30, because the gateway's documented Sunday week-anchor divergence makes temporal assertions unrepresentative. Monday through Saturday runs certify normally.
(d) Apply expect_week to every scenario whose input carries a week qualifier: the five named ones plus 'named weekday' if applicable, 'week plus time of day', the Chinese qualified-week scenario, and the cost-question scenario that opens with a vague next-week request. At least five scenarios must carry date expectations.
Do not delete or rename any scenario; the count stays at 30. Keep the existing PHI masking (the mask function) intact; dates MM/DD/YYYY must survive masking for the comparator, so parse before masking where needed but never print a full patient identifier.

OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md: '# Suite Upgrade' then '## Summary' (max 3 bullets), '## Assertions Changed' table, '## Runner Capabilities Added' table, '## What A Sunday Run Now Does', '## Assumptions'. Under 600 words.

You are adding one safety gate to a batch SMS sender. BOUNDARY: write only inside your task directory; never call an external API, never send anything, never git commit. You own exactly three output files: ./sms_recall_batch.py, ./test_sms_recall_batch.py, ./report.md. Copy both from ./source/ and edit the copies.

WHY. The temporal contract for this system documents a gateway week-anchor divergence that occurs only on Sundays, and the second red-team reviewer conditioned acceptance of that residual defect on outbound Sunday sends being HARD-BLOCKED IN CODE, not just by practice. See ./source/GEMINI-RULINGS.txt section R4. Today the only time gate is a 10:00-18:00 quiet-hours window that allows Sundays.

THE CHANGE. In the approve path of run(), before any send, refuse with a Refusal naming the reason when the practice-local day is Saturday or Sunday. Practice-local means the TIMEZONE constant already used by the quiet-hours check. The refusal message must say plainly that weekend outbound sends are blocked by policy, so an operator reading it knows it is intentional. --dry-run continues to work every day, it sends nothing. Do not touch the send payload, the ledger, suppression, enrichment, or anything else; the independent payload contract check runs against your file and must still pass.

TESTS. Add tests with 'sunday' or 'weekend' in their names proving: a clock returning a Sunday practice-local datetime causes run() with --approve to refuse before any /v1/sms/send call reaches the fake transport, and prints external_actions_taken=0; a Saturday likewise; a Monday clock with the same feed proceeds to exactly one send. Reuse the existing FakeHttp and feed helpers. Keep every existing test passing unmodified.

OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md: '# Sunday Send Block' then '## Summary' (max 3 bullets), '## Change' naming the exact function and condition, '## Tests Added' table, '## Assumptions'. Under 400 words.
